source.title: From Refusal Geometry to Safety Geometry: Harmfulness--Refusal Coupling under Dynamic Adversarial Fine-Tuning
source.authors: Wen-Hao Lan; Shan Li; Xin Lai; Mei-Qi Wu; Jun-Bin Yang; Hai-Hua Shen

record.tranche_reason: The study tests harmfulness and refusal carriers with causal interventions and behavioral readouts, but uses a dual-carrier protocol rather than the original single-direction, all-layer-and-position ablation method.
record.gate_note: The study measures harmfulness-minus-benign and refusal-minus-compliance carriers, their overlap, and effects of selected H/R interventions. It does not report an all-layer, all-position ablation of one refusal direction or harmless-prompt refusal after adding that direction. Table 1 and Table 4 include intervention outcomes; Table 2 reports trajectory outcomes. Cited results from other work are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study extracts a harmful-minus-benign difference-in-means carrier (H) and a refusal-vs-compliance carrier (R). It ablates and steers each, measuring HarmBench ASR. It also measures H/R overlap (principal angles, HRCIrepr). These bear on V1, because H is the V1 recipe at a single selected layer, and on V5, because harm and refusal are separated. The method differs from the original: single selected layers, a COSMIC-style R, and ASR as the outcome.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. Add the aligned-anchor finding: refusal-side carriers are causal bottlenecks (R ablation reopens ASR), whereas harmfulness-only ablation does not, and the two carriers are near-orthogonal. The main result is the R2D2 coupling-regime transition. Low coupling is not a safety score, and the work does not prove independent pathways or deployment-grade prediction.
record.recipe_differences: The study extracts a harmfulness carrier from harmful-versus-benign contrasts and a refusal carrier from refusal-versus-compliance contrasts, then measures overlap and tests selected H/R ablations and steering. It does not apply the original single refusal-direction ablation across every layer and position.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes are reported across aligned models, SFT versus R2D2 regimes, trajectory checkpoints, carrier type, intervention mode, and intervention strength. The authors note carrier-layer selection, checkpoint ordering, and matched unit-direction controls; controls are not matched to raw activation-delta norms. Only one completed Mistral training run per regime is reported.

fits_no_version.finding: Under R2D2 adversarial fine-tuning, H/R coupling drops from a plateau to a low value around steps 105–110. This co-occurs with reopened ASR, falling over-refusal and recovered utility; SFT shows low coupling with high ASR throughout.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adversarial safety training changes how tightly harmfulness and refusal representations are coupled, and that coupling tracks the robustness/over-refusal/utility state.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding the refusal carrier in SFT checkpoints raised ASR rather than refusal, but the outputs were degenerate (StrongREJECT 0.024, helpfulness 0).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Steering with refusal carriers in fine-tuned base models can produce generic disruption rather than induced refusal.

record.code_released: not stated; the paper says an artifact package will be deposited upon acceptance but gives no URL
record.problems: The main Mistral trajectory uses one completed run per regime; checkpoints are ordered trajectory states, not independent samples. Causal controls are matched unit directions, not raw activation-delta-norm matched. Intervention-level StrongREJECT and benign-utility follow-up covers selected rows rather than the full matrix. Benign utility uses a 60-prompt set, and sparse transfer is small-n and fixed-protocol rather than adaptive or black-box. The authors explicitly caution that the measures do not establish independent pathways or deployment-grade prediction.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 StrongREJECT values for all 10 anchors are omitted because the 60-row limit prioritizes HRCIrepr, ASR, XSTest refusal, benign helpfulness, aligned-anchor intervention comparisons, and the representative causal rows. Table 3 dense all-anchor correlation rows and Table 5 sparse-transfer correlation rows are also omitted; the authors characterize these as descriptive diagnostics, not standalone causal or deployment-prediction evidence. The intervention-level follow-up reports aggregate selected-target ASR 0.253 versus 0.207 for matched controls, empty-or-nonsensical StrongREJECT rate 0.833 and benign helpfulness 0.288 for selected targets, plus SFT steering ASR 0.3906 with StrongREJECT 0.024 and benign helpfulness 0; these aggregate and follow-up results are not extracted as individual model-checkpoint rows.

untested.parts: Ablation across all layers and positions; inducing refusal on harmless prompts by adding the direction; preservation of general capabilities under ablation; refusal rate as the direct outcome rather than HarmBench ASR.
No weight edits or abliterated released models.
Does not test whether jailbreaks suppress the direction or train against its ablation. R2D2 is analysed only for coupling.
No multi-direction, cone or affine analysis of refusal.
No transfer across languages, variants or base-to-instruct.
SFT and R2D2 trajectories are compared for H/R coupling, not for whether a single removable refusal direction exists.

missing.what: Selected carrier layers (Llama H at layer 31, R at 12; Qwen H at 15, R at 20). These bear on why the H direction fails under V1.
Mode-level causal-sweep summary: many R2D2 ablation modes do not exceed control maxima, and matched controls can have comparable effects. Stated in text only, without numbers.
Intervention-level follow-up across 8 selected targets: ASR 0.253 vs 0.207 for controls, empty-or-nonsensical rate 0.833, helpfulness 0.288. Declared in rows_left_out but needed to qualify r51–r58.
Intervention strength used for the aligned-anchor ablations is not stated.

record.verdict_notes: The H carrier is the harmful-minus-benign difference-in-means at a layer chosen for stable harmfulness validation, not for refusal. Its failure under ablation is therefore read as layer/contrast dependence (limits_scope), not a clean challenge to V1. R carrier rows are linked to V5 only, because V1 names the harmful-minus-harmless contrast. Table 4 rows are selected top rows, not representative. Text attributes R-side ASR reopening partly to degeneration. One Mistral run per regime; preprint with no released code.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests selected harmfulness-carrier interventions against HarmBench ASR, but not projection from every layer and position, refusal rates on harmful requests as a direct outcome, harmless refusal after adding the direction, or preservation of general capabilities after that specific intervention.
No weight-edit or released-model abliteration experiment is reported.
The attacks are not tested as suppressing the H/R carrier, and the study does not train against carrier ablation.
The study compares harmfulness and refusal carriers, not whether refusal itself is better represented by an affine set, cone, or multiple refusal directions.
The carriers are operational contrasts and the study explicitly does not establish independent neural pathways or a complete representation of harmfulness judgment and refusal decision.
No cross-language, base-to-instruct, or model-variant transfer test of the same direction is reported.
SFT and R2D2 trajectories are compared for H/R coupling, but the study does not test whether training determines the existence of one removable refusal direction.

source_check.notes: The Mistral checkpoints are the authors' single SFT and R2D2 runs, shared with an overlapping-author paper (arXiv:2604.27019), so do not count the two as independent evidence. Table 4 'reopening' is measured against control means only. The SFT and R2D2-step-500 target ASRs (0.14–0.39) sit below the unedited Table 2 ASRs (0.25–0.59), and the text doesn't say whether both use the same set. The text title (v3) is 'Tracking Harmfulness–Refusal Coupling under Dynamic Adversarial Fine-Tuning', not the record's title. One text-only result may bear on V7 and has no row: R2D2 ablation modes mostly stay at or below control maxima, while SFT R-side rows reopen most. There are no numbers for R-side rows in R2D2.

statements.correction: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct: H carrier selected at layer 15, R carrier at layer 20 (Table 1). H-only ASR 0.2625→0.2925. Layers where the ablation is applied are not stated in the main text.
statements.problem: differences_stated says this study ablates at one layer (15). The text gives 15 only as the H carrier's selected layer and doesn't state the ablation's layer scope.
Minor: the Mistral values come from the authors' own SFT and R2D2 runs from base Mistral-7B-v0.1, one run each. The angles are between top-k local H/R subspaces.

statements.correction: Table 1 gives point ASRs only: Llama 0.1675→H-only 0.1400, R-only 0.6825, R⊥H 0.6575. Qwen 0.2625→H-only 0.2925, R-only 0.4050, R⊥H 0.4250. No control or interval values for these rows.
statements.problem: The 'why' says matched controls and uncertainty, but the cited rows (Table 1, aligned anchors) report neither. Δcontrol appears only in the Mistral sweep (Table 4) and intervals only in the dense correlations (Table 3).

statements.correction: HRCIrepr = ½·Ccos + ½·Csub (Eq. 9). At R2D2 reference Ccos = 0.0977, Csub = 0.0370. The H and R carriers are taken at different selected layers and positions.
statements.problem: Says the study measures 'not cosine'. In fact HRCIrepr is half the H/R direction cosine plus half the mean squared principal-angle cosine.
Minor: 'does not reopen' holds cleanly for Llama only. On Qwen, H-only raised ASR slightly and the authors call it less clean.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Coupling and behavior varied by training regime: R2D2 moved from higher coupling with zero ASR and collapsed utility toward lower coupling with reopened ASR and recovered utility, while SFT remained high-ASR at low coupling (r11–r50). The study treats coupling as a diagnostic, not proof of separate mechanisms or a general safety score.
